digest.component_or_area: Source code comment linting and CI enforcement
propositions: Source code comments contain unresolvable commit SHAs, run IDs, job IDs, and dated incident narratives that become stale and unresolvable over time, creating maintainability debt.

A new block-level comment and docstring scanner detects rot-prone patterns: SHA-like hex strings (7+ chars), run/job/thread IDs (8+ digits after keyword), and dated incident narratives (date token + past-tense incident verb from enumerated set).

Detector accepts comments that cite ticket/epic/story/bug/rec/ADR IDs in grouped or word-triple-alias form, or use 'context: external' escape hatch for vendor-pinned references; it must not false-accept on current-state explanations or path names.

All detector-hit sites in the codebase must be remediated by either citing a resolvable ticket ID, dropping the rot-prone token while preserving durable prose, or replacing SHA narratives with behavioral descriptions findable via git log.

CI guard must be wired into the build workflow, block reintroduced rot-prone references with zero in-tree suppressions, and include unit tests covering false-positive gotchas identified in prototype (false-accept on aliases in path context and sentence-final aliases).
Policy guidance must be documented that source code comments convey current state and concise rationale, while the ticket system owns historical detail and incident narratives.
